display.title: Clean Language, and a Blizzard Trip to the Baal Shem Tov's Melave Malka
display.summary_short: Parshas Noach teaches us to speak in clean, positive language; then a Chassid who will not give up on the Baal Shem Tov's Melave Malka gets a ride through a blizzard from a surprising wagon driver.
display.summary_long: After the song 'I Believe in Hashem', the storyteller draws a lesson from Parshas Noach: the Torah spends extra words to say 'animals that are not pure' instead of 'impure', to teach us to use clean, positive language, as the Rebbe always did. Good thoughts and words create good angels. A Baal Shem Tov story shows how real words are: when a man in Mezhibuzh shouted that he would tear his rival apart like a fish, the Baal Shem Tov had his students hold hands and close their eyes, and they cried out at what they saw. Then the Alter Rebbe, shortly before his passing, reminds the Tzemach Tzedek not to hum a sad tune, because the face we show below is reflected Above; try to be happy, even if you have to start by pretending. After a word about keeping good resolutions, the final story follows Reb Moshe, who walks through the forest every Motzaei Shabbos to the Baal Shem Tov's Melave Malka. In a winter blizzard he falls into an icy pit, goes home to change, and sets out again. A wagon driver gives him a ride on condition that he sing along, and at the Melave Malka the Baal Shem Tov reveals who the driver really was.
display.lesson: Speak and think only good, positive words, and when something you are trying to do does not work the first time, try again; Hashem helps those who keep trying.

sources_cited.note: 'The animal that is not pure' instead of 'impure'.
The lesson of clean language from this verse; good thoughts and words create angels.
The Baal Shem Tov's vision story, 'we just heard a couple of days ago in Hayom Yom'.
The Rebbe's habit of avoiding negative words; making resolutions the right size.
The Alter Rebbe quoting the Maggid of Mezritch to the Tzemach Tzedek: as one's face below, so Above.
